W = Zq(p^f, N, names='a', type='capped-abs', print_mode='series'); A = PowerSeriesRing(W, 'z', L). Zq's default modulus is the Conway polynomial (verified against conway_polynomial and Nemo/Hecke).

E is passed as A(eisenstein_normalization(p, E)): the normalization returns a series over Frac(W) whose coercion into B = A[f_0, ...] fails over Zq in Sage 10.3; the normalized E is integral, so this is exact.

provenance.sign_convention: Sage: g0 = z0 - z1 (eta_R(z) = z - g0); nablaOK column k is the g0-coefficient of NF(-(z-g0)^k v^i). For odd p this equals the paper convention z1 = z0 + g0, nabla = theta o (eta_R - eta_L); for p = 2 the matrices differ by units (Sage g1 = -g1 - g0^2 in paper terms): compare cohomology only.
provenance.trust_note: Upstream KZPN hard-codes f = 1; these fixtures come from an in-memory sigma-patched copy. Lower trust than f = 1 Sage fixtures; validated by the self_checks below.
provenance.working_precision_rule: N = N_apriori_plan + margin, N_apriori_plan = 2T + 1 + (M_g+1) + sum_{s=p}^{i-1} n v_p(s!) + n C(i,2), margin = 2L + 10 unless --margin
provenance.nemo_check: julia version 1.12.7; using Nemo, Hecke; defining_polynomial(qadic_field(p, f; precision=10))

conventions.p_adic_numbers: decimal strings of representatives in [0, p^prec)
conventions.W_element: list of f decimal strings: coordinates in the basis 1, a, ..., a^(f-1) of Z_p[x]/(h_tilde), a = x the Conway generator; h_tilde is the Conway lift (low -> high)
conventions.E: E: exact integer coordinates reduced into [0, p^E_prec) with E_prec = N (the case working precision); E_exact_signed: the same exact integers with sign (e.g. E^sigma, E(az) have negative coordinates). E_normalized = E/(E(0)/p) as computed by Sage (per-coefficient absolute precision in E_normalized_prec).
conventions.polynomials: lists low -> high degree of W-elements
conventions.matrices: case["matrices"][name] for name in can0, phi0, can1, red, redN, nablaOK (same layout as sage_f1.json): {rows, cols, index_convention, entries (row-major W-elements), prec (absolute precision per entry as reported by Sage; exact zeros carry N)}. case["sigma_matrix_S"] is a Z_p-matrix: its entries are single decimal strings, not W-element lists
conventions.zp_expansion: W-linear A -> M(A) (block (r,c) = f x f matrix of multiplication by A[r][c], column j = coordinates of A[r][c]*a^j); sigma-semilinear Phi -> M(Phi)*(I kron S); the 1-based index of a^d * b_m is f*(m-1)+d+1
conventions.square_completions: over Zp capped-abs after expansion: nabla_R = M(redN) M(nablaOK) M(red)^-1; can-phi = M(can0) - M(phi0)(I kron S); N nabla = M(can1)^-1 nabla_R M(can0); can-phi^nabla = nabla_R (can-phi) (N nabla)^-1; d0 = [can-phi ; N nabla], d1 = [nabla_R, -(can-phi^nabla)]
conventions.cohomology: h1 = torsion of coker d0, h2 = coker d1, as sorted exponent lists (Z/p^a); [] = 0; H0 = 0 (Cor 2.14). K_{2i-1}(R; Z_p) = H1, K_{2i-2}(R; Z_p) = H2 for i >= 2.
conventions.paper_vs_sage_notation: paper n = Sage k (power of the uniformizer), i = weight, L = n*i = Sage Fprec
conventions.convention_dependence: can0, phi0, can1, red, redN are f-side matrices and do not depend on the g-side sign convention; nablaOK is in Sage's convention (see provenance.sign_convention)

can0.index_convention: Step 9 input: W-linear can: N^{>=i} -> Prism of R = O_K/pi^n. red.index_convention: Step 6 red: Prism_OK -> Prism_R on F-weights 1..L-1: entry [r][c] is the coefficient of the basis element of F-weight r+1 in NF_R(z^{c+1}) (Sage L706-717, OKtoOKmodpi0). Z_p expansion: M(red).
